units.rhetorical_move: opens on an imperative about stability
units.function: make the stakes a duty before the goal

original_instantiations: understanding the tensions is called imperative
the duty comes before any model is named

units.source_excerpt: Understanding the socioeconomic processes and tensions is called imperative.
units.reusable_pattern: Open by calling the understanding of the problem imperative.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften imperative into useful.

units.rhetorical_move: names three metrics with single letters
units.function: brand each metric with a letter

original_instantiations: income, education and equality each get a letter
the letters are used from then on

units.source_excerpt: From these parameters we generated three metrics, each branded with a letter.
units.reusable_pattern: Name a metric and assign it a single letter in the same sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not rename the letters.

units.rhetorical_move: says a metric both rewards and punishes
units.function: give a metric two opposing jobs

original_instantiations: the income metric rewards a higher per capita value
it punishes a wage gap that is too wide or too narrow

units.source_excerpt: The income metric favors higher per capita income and punishes a wage gap.
units.reusable_pattern: Define a metric by what it favors and what it punishes.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not keep only the reward.

units.rhetorical_move: joins two lenses with so as to
units.function: evaluate one thing through two lenses

original_instantiations: unemployment is read as an economic factor
the student ratio is read as a welfare factor

units.source_excerpt: The education metric reads unemployment one way and the student ratio another, so as to use both lenses.
units.reusable_pattern: Say a metric looks through two lenses, joined by so as to.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not collapse the two lenses.

units.rhetorical_move: reports the best population as a mean and a ratio
units.function: give the optimum as two numbers

original_instantiations: the best starting population has a stated mean age
it also has a stated ratio of two worker types

units.source_excerpt: Using our model, we found the best initial population had a stated mean age and a stated ratio.
units.reusable_pattern: Report an optimum as we found that plus two figures.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not round the stated figures.

units.rhetorical_move: ranks one result most important
units.function: close the summary on a superlative

original_instantiations: one recommendation is marked most important
it concerns a survey rather than a number

units.source_excerpt: Most importantly, a happiness survey can be utilized to build a collaborative society.
units.reusable_pattern: End a summary by marking one item most important.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a second most important item.

units.rhetorical_move: prints a full letterhead
units.function: give the letter a date, a name and an address

original_instantiations: the letter carries a date and a named director
a street address and a city follow the name

units.source_excerpt: The advisory is dated and addressed to a named director at a street address.
units.reusable_pattern: Head a policy letter with a date, a name and a postal address.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent an address the letter lacks.

units.rhetorical_move: opens with thanks and an exclamation
units.function: raise the register with punctuation

original_instantiations: thanks comes with an exclamation mark
the project is called humanity's greatest advancement

units.source_excerpt: Thank you for working with us to design a plan to colonize Mars.
units.reusable_pattern: Open the letter with thanks and an exclamation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not flatten the exclamation.

units.rhetorical_move: doubles a word by accident
units.function: leave the repeated article in place

original_instantiations: the article a is printed twice in a row
the sentence otherwise recommends a survey

units.source_excerpt: The sentence prints the article twice before strong.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep a doubled word as part of the letter's voice.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not silently delete the repeat.

units.rhetorical_move: borrows a famous call to open
units.function: start the section with a known phrase

original_instantiations: the section opens on a borrowed distress call
the agency's full name follows immediately

units.source_excerpt: The introduction opens by borrowing a well-known distress call.
units.reusable_pattern: Open a section by borrowing a phrase the reader already knows.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the borrowed phrase as original.

units.rhetorical_move: defines the mission in one sentence
units.function: state the mission as two maxima

original_instantiations: the mission is to create a sustainable society
it does so by maximizing output and happiness together

units.source_excerpt: The mission of the first population is to create a sustainable society by maximizing two things.
units.reusable_pattern: Define the mission as maximizing two named goods at once.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop one of the two goods.

units.rhetorical_move: restates the task in the team's own words
units.function: rephrase the brief as a task

original_instantiations: the group is tasked with policy recommendations
the recommendations must maximize output and happiness

units.source_excerpt: Our group is tasked with developing policy recommendations for the first population.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate the problem as a task the group was given.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add goals the restatement lacks.

units.rhetorical_move: names the three factors the policy must serve
units.function: bind the advice to three factors

original_instantiations: income, education and equality bound the advice
the advice must accommodate the project

units.source_excerpt: The goal is to consider income, education and equality as they relate to the project.
units.reusable_pattern: List the factors the recommendations must serve.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fourth factor.

units.rhetorical_move: states death as natural only
units.function: exclude every other cause of death

original_instantiations: agents die only of natural causes
disease and disaster are excluded by the assumption

units.source_excerpt: Residents die only naturally, with disease and disaster excluded.
units.reusable_pattern: State an assumption as an exclusion of every other cause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reintroduce an excluded cause later.

units.rhetorical_move: introduces a named example agent
units.function: make the formula concrete with a person

original_instantiations: a named agent of a stated age is introduced
her spouse is named in the same paragraph

units.source_excerpt: Consider another agent, a named woman of a stated age who is married.
units.reusable_pattern: Introduce a formula through a named person with an age.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the name.

units.rhetorical_move: says the probability peaks at one age
units.function: give the peak and its source

original_instantiations: the birth probability peaks at a stated age
the peak is credited to a citation

units.source_excerpt: The probability peaks at a stated age, as a citation shows, and is lower at both boundaries.
units.reusable_pattern: State where a probability peaks and cite the source.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not move the peak.

units.rhetorical_move: walks one agent through a lifecycle
units.function: narrate the model as one life

original_instantiations: one agent attends college, then searches for work
income follows only after a job is found

units.source_excerpt: Each agent progresses by attending college, searching for jobs, and earning income.
units.reusable_pattern: Explain a model by narrating one agent's stages in order.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reorder the stages.

units.rhetorical_move: compares a proportion to its Earth value
units.function: measure equality against a baseline planet

original_instantiations: the share of women in jobs is compared to Earth
the comparison stands for social equality

units.source_excerpt: The equality metric compares the proportion of women in jobs to their proportion on Earth.
units.reusable_pattern: Define equality as a comparison against a named baseline.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not change the baseline.

units.rhetorical_move: calls one value logically the best
units.function: promote a figure with an adverb

original_instantiations: one wage is called logically the best
the claim rests on the metric and the output gain

units.source_excerpt: Given the high metric and the large gain, one wage is logically the best value.
units.reusable_pattern: Call a value the best only after naming the two things that support it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the supports.

units.rhetorical_move: says a tax raises inequality while holding two things
units.function: state one cost and two benefits

original_instantiations: a progressive tax increases income inequality
it keeps investment high and debt low

units.source_excerpt: A progressive tax increased inequality while keeping investment high and debt low.
units.reusable_pattern: Describe a policy by the one thing it worsens and the two it protects.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide the cost.

units.rhetorical_move: hands unskilled work to machines
units.function: let automation free the workers

original_instantiations: unskilled jobs are given to automated devices
funded college keeps the workers employed anyway

units.source_excerpt: As technology advances, unskilled jobs can be given to automated devices.
units.reusable_pattern: Raise automation, then say funded education offsets it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the offset.

units.rhetorical_move: admits a measure is subjective
units.function: concede a metric cannot be measured

original_instantiations: the happiness index is called largely subjective
it therefore cannot be measured in the quantitative model

units.source_excerpt: The happiness index is largely subjective and thus cannot be accurately measured.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit a measure is subjective and say what follows from that.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not then treat the index as measured.

units.rhetorical_move: describes generations as waves
units.function: turn an age histogram into waves

original_instantiations: the age distribution shows distinct generation waves
the original wave is named and the later waves are new

units.source_excerpt: A distinct set of generation waves is visible in the age distribution.
units.reusable_pattern: Describe an age distribution as waves, and name which wave is which.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not mix up which wave is the original.

units.rhetorical_move: says every run reaches one steady state
units.function: claim convergence across all trials

original_instantiations: every population tested reaches the same steady state
in that state birth and death are roughly equal

units.source_excerpt: All populations tested eventually reach the steady state where birth and death are roughly equal.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim convergence by saying every tested case reaches one state.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim an untested case converges.

units.rhetorical_move: tells the reader what to notice
units.function: point at a feature of a figure

original_instantiations: the reader is told to notice a drop then a spike
the feature belongs to one named metric

units.source_excerpt: The caption tells the reader to notice the sudden drop and then the spike.
units.reusable_pattern: Direct the reader to one feature of a figure with the verb notice.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not describe features the caption does not name.

units.rhetorical_move: gives leave lengths for two parents
units.function: report two paired durations

original_instantiations: one parent's leave is a stated number of months
the other parent's leave is a shorter stated length

units.source_excerpt: We determined a leave length for one parent and a shorter one for the other.
units.reusable_pattern: Report two paired durations, naming who gets which.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not swap the two lengths.

units.rhetorical_move: says all selection processes are sustainable
units.function: qualify a whole table at once

original_instantiations: every selection process tested is called sustainable
the reason is that selection uses only three traits

units.source_excerpt: Since selection uses only age, sex and occupation, all the processes are highly sustainable.
units.reusable_pattern: Qualify a whole table with one since clause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not exempt one row silently.

units.rhetorical_move: warns against stuffing one type in
units.function: give the warning in quotation marks

original_instantiations: loading one worker type is warned against
the result is very high unemployment

units.source_excerpt: Simply loading one worker type into the population leads to very high unemployment.
units.reusable_pattern: Warn against one tempting choice and name its consequence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit the consequence.

units.rhetorical_move: tests emergency arrivals at six sizes
units.function: list the sizes that were tried

original_instantiations: six population sizes were sampled
each agent had an equal chance of either sex

units.source_excerpt: We sampled six population sizes, each with an equal chance of either sex.
units.reusable_pattern: State a sensitivity test as a list of sizes plus the sampling rule.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a size that was not tested.

units.rhetorical_move: says output grows linearly with population
units.function: state the shape of the relationship

original_instantiations: output increases linearly with population
the other characteristics stay comparable

units.source_excerpt: Output increases linearly with population, while other characteristics stay comparable.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the shape of one relationship and say the rest are comparable.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim linearity for the other characteristics.

units.rhetorical_move: reports one rate all populations share
units.function: give the value that every case converged to

original_instantiations: every population settled near one unemployment band
the band is stated as a range

units.source_excerpt: All populations eventually showed a stable unemployment rate inside one narrow band.
units.reusable_pattern: Report a value that every tested population reached.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not extend the band past the stated one.

units.rhetorical_move: flags infrastructure as unmodeled
units.function: name what the model leaves out

original_instantiations: infrastructure is not considered in the model
it must be reevaluated if a mass migration occurs

units.source_excerpt: Infrastructure is not considered and must be reevaluated if such a migration occurs.
units.reusable_pattern: Name an omitted factor and the condition that would make it matter.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the omitted factor as included.

units.rhetorical_move: contrasts the agent model with a continuous one
units.function: say what the other approach forces

original_instantiations: a continuous model forces broad generalization
the agent model reveals outcomes pure mathematics misses

units.source_excerpt: Unlike a continuous model, the agent approach reveals outcomes not quantifiable with pure mathematics.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim a strength by saying what the alternative forces you to do.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not insult the alternative beyond the text.

units.rhetorical_move: bounds the tested horizon
units.function: admit the test covered only part of the claim

original_instantiations: the model was rigorously tested for one stated span
beyond that span the claim rests on patterns holding

units.source_excerpt: We only rigorously tested the model for a stated span, and rely on patterns holding after that.
units.reusable_pattern: Separate the tested span from the claimed span.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the untested span as tested.

units.rhetorical_move: says varying characteristics cuts assumptions
units.function: tie dynamics to fewer assumptions

original_instantiations: letting characteristics vary reduces the assumptions
fewer assumptions mean fewer points that can break

units.source_excerpt: By allowing characteristics to vary, we reduce the number of assumptions.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify dynamic variables by the assumptions they remove.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the assumptions are gone entirely.

units.rhetorical_move: warns that small changes compound
units.function: name the horizon over which error grows

original_instantiations: small changes in the census data compound
the compounding is said to grow large over a stated span

units.source_excerpt: Relatively small changes in the data can compound into large variation over a stated span.
units.reusable_pattern: Warn that small input changes compound, and name the horizon.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit the horizon.

units.rhetorical_move: says the model is strictly economic
units.function: limit the model to one domain

original_instantiations: the model is strictly economic in nature
physical infrastructure is therefore left out

units.source_excerpt: The model is strictly economic, so it leaves out the physical infrastructure.
units.reusable_pattern: Limit the model to one domain and name what that excludes.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply the model covers the excluded domain.

units.rhetorical_move: admits the model is probabilistic
units.function: require repeated runs

original_instantiations: the same settings return slightly different values
multiple trials are therefore required

units.source_excerpt: The model returns slightly different values under the same settings, so multiple trials are required.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit a model is probabilistic and say how many runs that demands.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report a single run as the value.

units.rhetorical_move: admits families are absent
units.function: name the interactions left out

original_instantiations: family structure is not considered
transfers of income within a family are therefore missed

units.source_excerpt: The model does not consider family structure, so income transfers within a family are missed.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit an omission and name the interaction it leaves out.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent the missing interaction.

units.rhetorical_move: restates the task and the method
units.function: reprise the opening in the past tense

original_instantiations: the task is restated as modeling over two horizons
the method is restated as an agent-based model

units.source_excerpt: We were tasked with modeling the population over two stated horizons.
units.reusable_pattern: Open the conclusion by restating the task in the past tense.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not introduce a new result here.

units.rhetorical_move: repeats the headline numbers
units.function: give the same optima a second time

original_instantiations: the mean age and the worker ratio return
the wage and the two leave lengths return too

units.source_excerpt: We found the same mean age, the same ratio, and the same wage as in the summary.
units.reusable_pattern: Repeat the headline figures in the conclusion.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not change a figure between the two tellings.

units.rhetorical_move: closes on a borrowed send-off
units.function: end with a phrase the reader knows

original_instantiations: the conclusion ends on a borrowed send-off
the phrase replaces a formal summary

units.source_excerpt: The conclusion ends by borrowing a well-known send-off.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a paper by borrowing a phrase instead of summarizing.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the borrowed phrase as a result.

units.rhetorical_move: prints the model as code
units.function: let the procedures stand as the specification

original_instantiations: each procedure opens with the word to
the procedure name says what it computes

units.source_excerpt: The appendix gives the model as procedures, each opened by the word to.
units.reusable_pattern: Present a model as code whose procedure names state the computation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not rewrite the code as prose.

units.rhetorical_move: comments out a block instead of deleting it
units.function: keep the disabled code visible

original_instantiations: a block is disabled with comment marks
the disabled lines stay in the listing

units.source_excerpt: A block of the listing is disabled with comment marks but left in place.
units.reusable_pattern: Leave commented-out code in the listing.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not delete the commented lines.

units.rhetorical_move: numbers the sources in brackets
units.function: cite by a bracketed number

original_instantiations: each source is tagged with a bracketed number
the same number appears in the text

units.source_excerpt: Sources are tagged with bracketed numbers that reappear in the text.
units.reusable_pattern: Cite a source by a bracketed number.
prohibited_generalizations: The numbering belongs to this paper and does not transfer.
